h1: The 6 Best Printers for Dorm Rooms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Dorm Room Printers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six compact printers for dorm rooms compared on footprint, wireless setup, scanning, duplex printing and ink or cartridge costs.
summary: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 is the best printer for dorm rooms: wireless, duplex, print-copy-scan and a compact body for $50 to $100. The TS6520 adds an OLED display for shared rooms, the TR4720 has a document feeder for scanning, and the HP DeskJet 4355 is the budget all-in-one. The MT610Pro is an inkless backup.
intro: Dorm printers fail on boring details. One that needs a USB cable to your laptop, or a wide body that will not fit on a standard desk shelf, ends up in the closet by October. Setup matters more than speed in a room you share with a roommate and a hundred other devices. If a printer takes more than ten minutes to join the Wi-Fi, students give up and walk to the library.

We reviewed eight printers and kept six that suit a dorm. We ranked them on spec sheets and owner-reported use, focusing on size, wireless and phone printing, scanning, two-sided printing and how much ongoing ink or cartridge hassle each one brings. Footprint and weight carry real weight here, because the machine has to move in and out every year.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: Prints, copies, scans and duplexes in a body that fits a dorm desk.
products.description:
The TS4320 is a wireless color inkjet all-in-one that prints, copies and scans, with two-sided printing built in. It has a compact desktop footprint and a one-year limited warranty, and sells for $50 to $100. Duplex halves paper use on long readings, which cuts the number of reams a student lugs up the stairs.

It wins over the TS6520 because it covers the same everyday jobs in the same price range without paying for features a solo student seldom uses. It gives up the display of the pricier TS6520, so setup relies on the phone app. Against the HP DeskJet 4355, it adds duplex.

Choose it for essays, forms and the occasional scan. The caveat is that inkjet cartridges add up and there is no screen for menus. Look elsewhere if you share the printer with several roommates.
products.idealFor: Most dorm students who want one all-round printer.
products.skipIf: A shared printer needs a screen for menus.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED screen makes a shared printer far less confusing.
products.description:
The TS6520 adds a 1.42 inch OLED display to a wireless color inkjet all-in-one with duplex printing and copy and scan functions. The design stays compact and it sells for $50 to $100. A small screen matters in a shared room because anyone can check status, clear a paper warning or change settings without installing an app.

It ranks just under the TS4320 only because most solo students never use the screen, and it sits in the same price range. For roommates, the display lets anyone check status or change settings without the app. Against the TR4720, it is smaller and adds duplex.

Pick it when two or more people share the machine. The caveat is that the screen is small. If you are the only user, the TS4320 does the same work without the extra feature. Skip it if you live alone.
products.idealFor: Shared dorm rooms with several users.
products.skipIf: You live alone and rarely touch settings.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: An automatic document feeder turns multi-page scanning into a one-step job.
products.description:
The TR4720 pairs wireless printing with an auto document feeder, built-in fax and mobile printing. It prints, scans, copies and faxes, comes in a white finish, and sells for $50 to $100. A feeder takes a stack of pages in one pass, so scanning a signed lease or lab notes takes seconds instead of minutes of lid lifting.

It ranks third because the feeder makes it bulkier than the TS-series models, which matters on a small desk. In return you can load a stack of signed pages and scan them without opening the lid for each sheet. Fax is a dated extra that most dorm users will never touch.

Best for students who scan lease paperwork, forms or lab notes often. The caveat is the larger body. If you mostly print, the TS4320 saves space. Skip it if desk space is very tight.
products.idealFor: Students who scan multi-page documents regularly.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A full wireless all-in-one that keeps the starting cost low.
products.description:
The HP DeskJet 4355 prints, scans and copies wirelessly and includes a three-month Instant Ink trial. It is a compact home design with AI-capable features listed, and sells for $50 to $100. Instant Ink bills by pages instead of cartridges, so a student who prints in bursts pays little during quiet weeks.

It ranks fourth because the listing does not mention duplex printing, which the Canon models above offer. The Instant Ink trial can lower early ink costs, but it is a subscription you need to manage after the trial, or ink supplies lapse. Against the TS3720, it adds the ink plan.

A good fit for budget-minded students who want a full machine without extra frills. The caveat is missing duplex and subscription upkeep. Skip it if two-sided printing is a priority.
products.idealFor: Budget students who want a full all-in-one.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS3720 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: The lightest, simplest Canon, easy to pack at semester's end.
products.description:
The TS3720 is a basic wireless color inkjet all-in-one with a compact, lightweight body in white. It prints, scans and copies and focuses on plain home printing. It sells for $50 to $100. Light weight is the point: it is the easiest of the Canons to carry up a staircase and pack at semester's end.

It sits below the TS4320 because it drops the duplex support and extras listed on that model. The upside is bulk, since it is the simplest to carry. Against the DeskJet 4355, it has no ink trial, but it is about as small and has the same basic jobs.

Good for students who change rooms each year and print only occasionally. The caveat is a basic feature set with no duplex listed. If your course load is print-heavy, the TS4320 saves paper and time. Skip it if you print large volumes.
products.skipIf: You print large volumes of coursework.

products.name: Inkless Portable Printer for Travel (MT610Pro)
products.verdict: No ink, no toner, just a thermal backup for occasional pages.
products.description:
The MT610Pro is a Bluetooth thermal printer that needs no ink or toner cartridges. It prints Letter and A4 at 300 DPI, works with iOS, Android and laptops, and sells for $50 to $100. Thermal printing heats special paper, so there is no cartridge to dry out over summer break.

It ranks last because it is not a copier or scanner, and thermal output suits plain documents rather than color work. Its advantage is size and zero cartridge shopping. Against the Canon all-in-ones, it replaces scanning and copying with pure portability.

Best as a lightweight backup for students who rely mostly on campus print stations. The caveat is monochrome-only output and no scan or copy. If you need scanning or color, one of the Canon all-in-ones is the better choice.
products.idealFor: Students who mostly use campus printing.
products.skipIf: You need scanning or color output.

whatMatters.detail: A dorm desk shelf is often narrower than a standard printer, and a heavy machine is hard to move at semester's end. Measure the space and compare it with the listing dimensions. Compact and lightweight wording in the specs is a helpful signal, as on the TS3720, and allow room for the open lid and paper tray too, since both extend past the body.

Wireless printing lets you send documents from a laptop or phone without a cable. In a shared room this avoids swapping cords between roommates. Check the listing for Wi-Fi or Bluetooth and for mobile printing support. Also ask your campus IT about device registration, since some dorm networks block printers. Ask before you buy, not after.

Duplex means the printer prints on both sides of the paper automatically. It halves your paper use on long readings and makes thick packets easier to handle. Look for the word duplex or 2-sided in the specs, since it is missing on some cheaper models like the DeskJet 4355 and TS3720.

A flatbed scanner handles single sheets, while an auto document feeder takes a stack. For lease forms or signed pages a feeder saves minutes each time. Check whether the listing mentions a feeder, as the TR4720 does, or only a flatbed, and think about how often you will scan more than a page. A feeder also helps copy double-sided forms.

Inkjets are cheap to buy, but replacement cartridges add up, and subscriptions bill monthly. Inkless thermal printers like the MT610Pro avoid cartridges but only print simple documents. Decide how much you really print before choosing, and count the yearly ink cost, not just the price of the printer. Paper adds up too.

howToChoose.intro: How often you print decides how much machine you need.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Inkjets print in color, scan and copy, but need cartridges. The Canon TS4320, TS6520, TR4720, TS3720 and the HP DeskJet 4355 are all inkjet all-in-ones.

cards.label: Inkless thermal
cards.text: Thermal printers use heat on special paper, so there are no cartridges, but they cannot scan or print color. The MT610Pro is the only one here.

howToChoose.note: Most students should choose an inkjet unless printing is rare.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Mobile and tablet printing support plus wireless setup so you can print without a laptop.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon TR4720 lists mobile printing support outright, and the MT610Pro works with iOS and Android over Bluetooth.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Several people share the printer, which favors the Canon TS6520 display, or you scan stacks, which favors the TR4720 feeder.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print rarely. The HP DeskJet 4355 or Canon TS3720 cover basics, and the MT610Pro skips cartridges completely.

faq.q: Do dorm printers need a cable?
faq.a: Not the wireless ones. The Canon models and the HP DeskJet 4355 join your Wi-Fi, while the MT610Pro uses Bluetooth. Check that your dorm network allows device connections before buying, because some block printers, and a registration step may be needed for the TS4320 or TR4720.

faq.q: What is the most common buying mistake?
faq.a: Buying on price without checking size. A printer that does not fit your desk shelf becomes floor clutter, so measure first, then compare the TS3720 and TS4320 on footprint. Check the shelf depth, since paper trays stick out.

faq.q: Is the TS6520 worth it over the TS4320?
faq.a: Only for shared rooms. The display helps roommates manage settings, but a solo student gets the same prints from the cheaper TS4320. Weigh the screen against how many people use the machine. Roommates tend to cause the most paper jams.

faq.q: How do I set up a wireless printer in a dorm?
faq.a: Use the manufacturer's phone app to join the printer to your Wi-Fi, then add it on your laptop. Some campus networks need a device registration step first, so do that before the first print.

faq.q: How do I keep ink costs down?
faq.a: Print in draft mode for notes, use duplex printing and avoid full-color pages. The HP Instant Ink trial can help early on, but track the plan after it ends. Buy a spare cartridge before finals week.

faq.q: Can an inkless printer replace a normal one?
faq.a: For plain text documents, yes. The MT610Pro cannot scan, copy or print color, so most students will still want an inkjet like the TS4320 for forms and projects. Keep the thermal one for quick drafts.

finalTake: Buy the Canon TS4320 for a solo dorm. Take the TS6520 when roommates share the machine, the TR4720 if you scan stacks of paperwork, and the DeskJet 4355 for the lowest start-up cost. The TS3720 is the light one for moving, and the MT610Pro a thermal backup only. Measure your shelf and test the Wi-Fi setup before ordering.
